status_note: Live and battle-tested: this exact image runs in a production AWS Nitro enclave guarding real Telegram accounts. Not a development, staging, or testnet build. The release is commit-pinned and reproducible; trust comes from rebuilding it and matching the PCR0 below, plus the live in-browser attestation.
gateway_commit_repo: github.com/Danimal01/enclave-gateway (THIS repository) — resolve gateway_commit/the tag here, not elsewhere; tag v1.0.2 is the source that builds to pcr0_g.
allowlist_sha256_preimage: IMPORTANT: allowlist_sha256 is INTENTIONALLY DIFFERENT from files[].sha256 below and is NOT supposed to equal it (this is not a mismatch). allowlist_sha256 = sha256 over the UTF-8 string '// FILE tg-chokepoint.mjs\n' concatenated with the file's bytes -- the attestation-binding digest the live attestation binds and the how-it-works page verifies. files[].sha256 = the plain `sha256sum tg-chokepoint.mjs`. Two verifiers, two values, same file.

files.name: tg-chokepoint.mjs
files.note: raw sha256 of the file bytes; matches `sha256sum tg-chokepoint.mjs`. Intentionally DIFFERS from the top-level allowlist_sha256 (the attestation-binding digest) -- see allowlist_sha256_preimage.

binaries.name: kmstool_enclave_cli
binaries.source: aws-nitro-enclaves-sdk-c v0.4.5 (commit cd61b61) with patches/apply-kmstool-context-patch.py applied; built via containers/Dockerfile.al2 --target kmstool-enclave-cli

reproducible_note: umask-independent: a 644 and a 664 source context build the IDENTICAL PCR0 (the Dockerfile canonicalizes every COPYed file's mode; .gitattributes pins LF). The three host-staged binaries above are pinned by sha256 so a verifier can confirm them. Build on any host and match.
transparency: To verify: check out tag v1.0.2 of THIS repository, rebuild per BUILD.md, and confirm the PCR0 matches pcr0_g. The tag is the exact source that builds to pcr0_g.

attestation.note: A live AWS Nitro enclave running this exact image attests PCR0_G above (the live artifact is authoritative for the current module id and timestamp). The capability allowlist (tg-chokepoint.mjs) is account-management only: no message, chat, file, or contact method.

note: Production release v1.0.2: disconnect-execution. When a user disconnects an armed account, the enclave now completes it end to end -- it re-verifies the signed disconnect envelope, signs its OWN Telegram session out (auth.LogOut, removing the guard device from the user's account), terminalizes the State Authority (ARMED->TERMINAL), and finalizes the link to 'disconnected'. The prior build had no post-arm disconnect path, so an armed disconnect stalled at 'disconnecting'. The allowlist CAPABILITY SET is UNCHANGED from v1.0.1 (auth.LogOut was already in the armed allowlist, gated by a signed disconnect at the policy head); allowlist_sha256 and files[].sha256 are byte-identical to v1.0.1. Deterministic, umask-independent reproducibility.
